Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 6 Current Affairs Study PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS CABINET APPROVALS Cabinet Approves Rs 1 Lakh Crore UCF and Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 In February 2026, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, has approved two major initiatives aimed at bolstering urban infrastructure financing and strengthening India’s startup ecosystem: the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) with a Rs 1 lakh crore central assistance and the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 (FoF 2.0) with a Rs 10,000 crore corpus. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Cabinet approvals for two major initiatives ✓ Approval-1: Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) o Total Corpus: Rs 1 Lakh Crore o Timeline: FY26–FY31, extendable up to FY34 o Expected Outcome: To accelerate Investments (around Rs 4 lakh crore) over the next 5 years o New Scheme Approved: Credit Repayment Guarantee Scheme (Rs 5,000 crore corpus) o Target Cities: 4,223 cities ✓ Approval-2: Setting up of the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 (Startup India FoF 2.0) o Outlay: Rs 10,000 crore o Purpose: To mobilize venture capital for the startup ecosystem of the country o Launched Under: Startup India Initiative (2016) About Urban Challenge Fund (UCF): Overview: The newly approved fund will be operational from Financial Year 2025-26 (FY26) to FY 2030- 31 (FY31), with an extendable implementation period up to FY34. • It aims to promote market-linked urban infrastructure development and is expected to catalyse investments of approximately Rs 4 lakh crore over the next five years. Funding Structure: Under the UCF, Central Assistance (CA) will cover 25% of the project cost, while minimum 50% of funding have to be mobilised from market sources such as: municipal bonds, bank loans and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs). • And, the remaining amount will be funded by states, Union Territories (UTs), Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) or other sources. Selection Process: The projects will be selected through a transparent and competitive challenge-based framework, ensuring support to transformative impact and reform-oriented proposals. Project Verticals: The new UCF will support projects across 3 key verticals: Cities as Growth Hub, Creative Redevelopment of Cities and Water and Sanitation. Coverage: The UCF will cover all cities with population above 10 lakh or more (2025 estimates); all State and UT capitals not covered above; and major industrial cities with a population of 1 lakh or more. • It will support all ULBs in hilly states, North-Eastern (NE) states, and smaller ULBs with population below 1 lakh under the Credit Repayment Guarantee Scheme. The Government of India (GoI) also clarified that ‘in principle all cities will be covered under UCF Reform-linked funding framework’. Credit Repayment Guarantee Scheme: The Cabinet has also approved a dedicated Rs 5,000 crore corpus for Credit Repayment Guarantee Scheme.

Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 7 Current Affairs Study PDF • It aims to enhance the creditworthiness of 4223 cities including Tier-II and Tier-III cities, particularly for first-time access to market finance. • Under this newly approved scheme, smaller Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) (with population below 1 lakh) and cities in North Eastern and hilly states will get a central guarantee of up to Rs 7 crore or 70% of the loan amount (whichever is lower) for 1st-time borrowing, while for subsequent projects, the central guarantee will extend up to Rs 7 crore or 50% of the loan amount. • Initially, the scheme will support projects of minimum Rs 20 crore and Rs 28 crore for subsequent projects in smaller cities. About Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 : Overview: The Union Cabinet has also approved the establishment of the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 (FoF 2.0) with total budget outlay of Rs 10,000 crore, aimed to mobilize venture capital for the startup ecosystem of the country. Launched under: It was launched under the wider Startup India initiative, launched in 2016. FFS 1.0: The new initiative is built on the performance of the FFS 1.0, launched in 2016. • Under FFS 1.0, the GoI has committed an entire Rs 10,000 crore to 145 Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) which have invested over Rs 25,500 crore in over 1,370 startups nationwide in sectors like: agriculture, Artificial Intelligence (AI), robotics, e-commerce, among others. Key Features: Startup India FoF 2.0 will have a targeted, segmented funding approach to support: • Deep-tech and tech-driven innovative manufacturing, empowering early-growth stage founders, national reach, and addressing high-risk capital gaps and bolstering India’s domestic venture capital base. Alignment: It is with the national vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047, the Fund underscores the GoI’s commitment to empowering entrepreneurs, fostering innovation, and unlocking the full potential of India’s startup ecosystem. Cabinet Approvals On February 14, 2026 In February 2026, The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved three railway expansion projects worth about Rs.18,509 crores. • The Union Cabinet has also approved proposals to shift key central ministries from North Block and South Block to newly constructed buildings Seva Teerth and Kartavya Bhavans in New Delhi, Delhi. Exam Hints: ✓ Approval 1: Union cabinet approved three railway expansion projects ✓ Value: Rs.18,509 crores ✓ Cabinet Chair: PM Narendra Modi ✓ Rail Routes: Delhi-Ambala, Kasara-Manmad, Ballari-Hosapete ✓ Distance: 389 Km ✓ Approval 2: Shifting key Ministries to Seva Teerth and Kartavya Bhavans ✓ Where? In New Delhi, Delhi ✓ Ministries: MoF, MHA, MoD, MEA, PMO About the Three Multitracking Railway Projects: Overview: Union Cabinet approved three multitracking projects, covering approximately 389 Kilometre (Km) across four states such as Delhi, Haryana, Maharashtra, and Karnataka, and targeted for completion by Financial Year 2030-31 (FY31). Approved Routes: The projects include addition of third and fourth line to the Delhi-Ambala (Haryana) to ease passenger congestion and improve freight flow towards northern states.

Congestion Reduction: Around 3,902 villages, with a population of nearly 97 lakh people, will benefit from the project, as the additional railway lines will reduce congestion, improve train speeds, enhance service reliability, and boost freight movement. Cabinet Approved Proposal to Shift Key Ministries to Seva Teerth and Kartavya Bhavans: Overview: The Union Cabinet approved proposals to shift key central ministries from North Block and South Block to newly constructed buildings named “Seva Teerth” and “Kartavya Bhavans”, as part of the Central Vista Redevelopment Project in New Delhi. About the North Block and South Block: It is located on Raisina Hill and has served as the administrative nerve centre of the Government of India (GoI). It was designed by British architect Edwin Lutyens and built during the British colonial period. • It houses the Ministry of Finance (MoF), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Ministry of Defence (MoD), Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). About Seva Teerth & Kartavya Bhavans: Modern Infrastructure: They are designed to provide digitally integrated smart offices with energy- efficient, eco-friendly systems, advanced security infrastructure, and spacious, well-planned workplaces. Enhanced Coordination: The initiative aims to bring departments under one coordinated system, improve inter-ministerial coordination, reduce logistical delays, and reduce rental and maintenance costs. Significance: The move aims to improve administrative efficiency, achieve cost rationalization, ensure infrastructure modernization, and promote citizen-centric symbolism. Name Significance: The name “Seva” refers to Service and Kartavya indicates Duty. About Haryana: Chief Minister (CM) – Nayab Singh Saini Governor – Professor Ashim Kumar Gosh Capital – Chandigarh Wildlife Sanctuary (WLS) – Kalesar WLS, Bir Shikargah WLS CCEA Approved Rs 11,000 Crore Highway Projects in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Telangana In February 2026, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved a series of Highway projects worth more than Rs 11,000 crore in 3 states namely, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Telangana. • The CCEA also approved the construction of India’s 1st underwater twin tube road-cum-rail tunnel project with estimated Cost of Rs 18,662 crore under Brahmaputra river in Assam. • The approved projects include road widening, rehabilitation and new 4-lane stretches aimed to boost freight movement and regional connectivity. Total Cost: The newly approved tunnel project will be developed at an estimated cost of Rs 18,662 crore on the Engineering- Procurement- Construction (EPC) model. Structure: The project involves the construction of a 33.7 kilometer (km)-long 4-lane access-controlled greenfield Highway, including a 15.79 km twin-tube tunnel. Boost Connectivity: The stretch will connect Gohpur on National Highway (NH)-15 to Numaligarh on NH- 715, thereby reducing the travel distance between two Assam cities (Gohpur and Numaligarh) from existing 240 kms to just 34 kms. Rehabilitation and Upgradation of NH-160A in Maharashtra: Approval: The CCEA approved the rehabilitation and upgradation of the Ghoti-Trimbak (Mokhada)- Jawhar-Manor-Palghar section of NH-160A in Maharashtra. Total Cost: 154.635 km-long project will be developed at an estimated cost of Rs 3,320.38 crore on the EPC mode. Widening of NH: Under this project, the NH will be developed as a two-lane corridor with paved shoulders, with select urban stretches, particularly between Manor and Palghar. Connectivity: The upgraded highway will connect key infrastructure, including the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, Mumbai-Nagpur Samruddhi Mahamarg, NH-848 and NH-48. 4-lanning of Key NH-56 Stretches in Gujarat: Approval: The CCEA approved the 4-laning of 107.67 km- long NH-56 in Gujarat. NH-56: The newly approved project is a part of NH-56 which originates at Nimbahera in Rajasthan and passes through Dahod district in Gujarat, Alirajpur district in Madhya Pradesh (MP) and then re-enters Gujarat near Chhota Udepur district, ending at its junction with NH-48 near Vapi. Cost: The upgradation of NH-56 will be done at a cost of Rs 4,583.64 crore under the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM). Structure: The newly approved project involves the construction of 4-lane sections from Dhamasiya to Bitada/ Movi (47.6 km) and Nasarpore to Malotha (60.21 km) Widening of NH-167 to 4-Lanes in Telangana: Approval: The CCEA approved the widening of the 80.01 km-long NH-167 stretch from Gudebellur to Mahbubnagar to 4-lane standards in Telangana. Cost: The approved project, part of the Hyderabad-Panaji Economic Corridor, will be developed at an estimated cost of Rs 3,175.08 crore under the HAM through the NH (O) scheme. Significance: The proposed project is expected to benefit Narayanpet and Mahbubnagar districts in

Multimodal Integration: The corridor will integrate with two major NHs (NH-150 and NH-167N), boosting connectivity to key economic, social, and logistics nodes across Telangana. Cabinet Approves Proposal to Rename the State of ‘Kerala’ as ‘Keralam’ On February 25 2026, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved a proposal to officially change the name of the state of ‘Kerala’ to ‘Keralam’, during its first meeting held at the newly inaugurated Seva Teerth office complex in New Delhi, Delhi. • The Cabinet also approved the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for raw jute for the 2026-27 marketing season and procurement under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) for Rabi 2026 crops. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Cabinet Approved the renaming of Kerala as ‘Keralam’ and fixed MSP for Raw Jute ✓ Approval 1: Rename Kerala as ‘Keralam’ • Purpose: Reflect state identity in Malayalam; align with 1956 reorganisation. • Amendment: Amends First Schedule (state name) & Fourth Schedule (Rajya Sabha seats) • Constitution: Article 3 ✓ Approval 2: MSP for Raw Jute • Price: Rs 5,925/quintal for 2026–27 • Nodal Agency: Jute Corporation of India (JCI) Renaming of Kerala to Keralam: Approval: The approval was followed by unanimous resolutions passed by the Kerala Legislative Assembly in August 2023 and June 2024. Procedure: Under Article 3 of the Constitution of India, the President refers the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 to the State Legislature for its views before it is introduced in Parliament, after which it must be passed by a simple majority in both Houses and receive Presidential assent. Amendment: The change requires modification of the First Schedule (listing states) and consequential updates to the Fourth Schedule (allocation of Rajya Sabha seats) of the Constitution. Basis: The name ‘Keralam’ reflects the state’s identity in the Malayalam language and aligns with its linguistic reorganisation on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. Clearance: The proposal was examined by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and approved by Union Minister Amit Shah, MHA, after which the draft Cabinet Memorandum was sent to the Ministry of Law and Justice (MoL&J), whose Department of Legal Affairs (DLA) and Department of Legislative Affairs (DOLA) concurred with the proposal. About Article 3: Authority: Article 3 of the Constitution of India empowers Parliament to form new States and alter the area, boundaries, or name of any existing State by law. Procedure: A Bill for such change can be introduced only on the recommendation of the President of India, who must refer it to the concerned State Legislature for expressing its opinion within a specified timeframe. Precedent: In 2011, Odisha was renamed from Orissa under the Orissa (Alteration of Name) Act, while the proposal to rename West Bengal (WB) as “Bangla” remains pending. Approval of MSP for Raw Jute 2026–27: Approval: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by PM Narendra Modi, fixed the MSP of Raw Jute (TD-3 grade, Fair quality) at Rs 5,925 per quintal (qtl) for the 2026–27 marketing season.

# Page 11^page=11
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 11 Current Affairs Study PDF • The price marks a rise of Rs 275 per quintal over 2025–26 and a 2.5-fold increase from Rs 2,400 per quintal in 2014–15 to Rs 5,925 in 2026–27. Return: The MSP ensures a 61.8% return over the all-India weighted average cost of production, in line with the 1.5 times cost principle announced in the Union Budget 2018–19. Nodal Agency: The Jute Corporation of India (JCI) will continue as the nodal agency for Price Support Operations (PSO), with losses reimbursed by the Central Government. Framework: MSP is announced by the Government of India (GoI), based on recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) and approval of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), to ensure remunerative prices and protect farmers from market volatility. About Jute: Jute is a biodegradable natural vegetable fibre obtained from plants of the genus Corchorus (Corchorus spp.), popularly known as the ‘Golden Fibre’ for its silky shine and golden colour. Production: India is the world’s largest producer of jute, followed by Bangladesh and China, with major cultivation in West Bengal (WB), Bihar, and Assam. About Kerala: Kerala, in southwestern India along the Malabar Coast, was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act 1956, by merging regions with a shared Malayalam linguistic and cultural identity. Chief Minister (CM)- Pinarayi Vijayan Governor– Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar Capital – Thiruvananthapuram Stadium – Trivandrum International Stadium; Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium Union Cabinet Approvals on February 24, 2026: Major Infrastructure, Metro, Airport & Rail Projects On 24th February 2026, the Union Cabinet of India, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved multiple projects to strengthen national infrastructure, energy, and transport connectivity. • Key decisions included enhanced delegation of powers to Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID), extension of the North–South corridor from Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) to Shahpur under Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation Limited (GMRC) at an estimated cost of Rs. 1,067.35 crore, development of a civil enclave at Srinagar Airport (Jammu and Kashmir, J&K) worth Rs. 1,677 crore, and approval of three railway multitracking projects valued at Rs. 9,072 crore. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Cabinet Approval of infrastructure projects across Power, Metro, Aviation, and Railways. ✓ Approvals: POWERGRID delegation, Metro extension, Srinagar Civil Enclave, and three railway multi-tracking projects ✓ Enhance Powers for POWERGRID: • Investment: Increased to Rs. 7,500 crore • Project Access: HVDC and UHVAC transmission projects • Target: 500 GW non-fossil-based power target ✓ Gujarat Metro Rail Extension: • Extension: Extension of the North-South corridor from GIFT City to Shahpur (Gujarat), spanning 3.33 kilometers (km) • Cost: Rs. 1,067.35 crore ✓ Srinagar Airport Civil Enclave: • Cost: Rs. 1,677 crore • Operated by: AAI ✓ Railway Multitracking Projects:

# Page 12^page=12
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 12 Current Affairs Study PDF • Cost: Rs. 9,072 crore • Projects: Gondia–Jabalpur Doubling (Maharashtra–Madhya Pradesh, MP), Punarakh–Kiul 3rd and 4th line (Bihar), and Gamharia–Chandil 3rd and 4th line (Jharkhand). • Support: Pradhan Mantri Gati Shakti National Master Plan (PMGS-NMP) Enhanced Powers for POWERGRID: Approval: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved an enhanced delegation to POWERGRID in accordance with the existing guidelines dated 4 February 2010 issued by the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) under Ministry of Finance (MoF), governing delegation of powers for Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs). Investment Limit: The permissible equity investment per subsidiary was increased from Rs. 5,000 crore to Rs. 7,500 crore, while retaining the existing 15% net worth cap. Project Access: POWERGRID can participate in bids for High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) and Ultra High Voltage Alternating Current (UHVAC) transmission projects. Objective: Facilitate evacuation of Renewable Energy(RE) to achieve India’s 500 Gigawatt (GW) non- fossil-based power target and enhance competition in Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB). Strategic Impact: The enhanced powers enable POWERGRID to expand investments in its core business, support RE integration, and ensure affordable, clean energy for consumers. Sector Outlook: India’s transmission sector is projected to require nearly Rs. 9.2 lakh crore by 2032 for grid modernization and renewable energy integration. Gujarat Metro Rail Extension: Project: The Union Cabinet approved the extension of the metro corridor from GIFT City to Shahpur, spanning 3.33 kilometers (km) with three elevated stations. Cost: Estimated project cost is Rs. 1,067.35 crore with a completion timeline of approximately four years. Executing Agency: Managed by GMRC, a 50:50 joint venture(JV) between the Government of India (GoI) and the Government of Gujarat. Ridership: Expected to benefit around 23,702 passengers by 2029 and 58,059 passengers by 2041. Connectivity: Strengthens linkages between Ahmedabad(Gujarat) and GIFT City(Gujarat), benefiting multinational companies, educational institutions, and commercial centres. Background: Ahmedabad Metro Phase-I and Phase-II have been operational since September 2022 and January 2026, with a daily ridership of about 1,60,000 passengers. Srinagar Airport Civil Enclave: Approval: The CCEA approved the development of a Civil Enclave at Srinagar International Airport, Budgam Airbase, J&K at an estimated cost of Rs. 1,677 crore. Terminal: A new state-of-the-art terminal building spanning 71,500 square meters (sq.m), including 20,659 sq.m of existing structure, will be constructed. Capacity: Designed to handle 2,900 passengers during peak hours and an annual capacity of 10 million passengers per annum (MPPA). Apron & Parking: The expanded apron will have 15 aircraft parking bays, including 1 widebody (Code E), and a multi-level car parking facility for 1,000 cars. Security: The Civil Enclave will be operated by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) within the Budgam Airbase of the Indian Air Force (IAF), with barracks for security personnel. Sustainability: Incorporates advanced water harvesting, maximized natural lighting, use of eco-friendly local materials, and is targeted for a 5-star GRIHA (Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment) rating. Impact: The project is expected to boost tourism, economic growth, employment, and improve connectivity to Dal Lake, Shankaracharya Temple, and Mughal Gardens in J&K.

# Page 13^page=13
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 13 Current Affairs Study PDF Railway Multitracking Projects: Approval: The CCEA also approved three multitracking projects under the Ministry of Railways (MoR) at a total cost of Rs. 9,072 crore. Projects: The approved projects include the Gondia–Jabalpur Doubling (Maharashtra–Madhya Pradesh, MP), Punarakh–Kiul 3rd and 4th line (Bihar), and Gamharia–Chandil 3rd and 4th line (Jharkhand), covering 307 km across eight districts and benefiting 5,407 villages and approximately 98 lakh people. Freight Capacity: The projects will increase freight traffic by 52 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA), supporting transportation of coal, steel, iron ore, cement, fertilizers, and foodgrains. Tourism Connectivity: Improved rail connectivity will benefit key destinations including Kachnar Shiv Temple, Kanha National Park (NP), Pench National Park (NP), Dhuandhar Waterfall, Bargi Dam, and Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary (WLS). Environmental Benefit: The projects are expected to reduce oil imports by 6 crore litres and lower Carbon Dioxide (CO2) emissions by 30 crore kg, equivalent to the plantation of one crore trees. Alignment: The initiatives support the Pradhan Mantri Gati Shakti National Master Plan (PMGS-NMP), enhancing multimodal connectivity, logistic efficiency, and sustainable transportation. About Pradhan Mantri Gati Shakti National Master Plan (PMGS-NMP): Launch: PMGS-NMP was launched in October 2021 by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (MoC&I). Outlay: The initiative has an investment of Rs. 100 lakh crore over five years. Nodal Ministry: Executed through the Logistics Division of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), MoC&I. Digital Tool: Planning and monitoring facilitated by Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N), Gandhinagar, Gujarat. Pillars: Built on six pillars: Comprehensiveness, Prioritization, Optimization, Synchronization, Analytical, Dynamic, to enhance connectivity and resource efficiency. About Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID): Chairman & Managing Director (CMD) – Ravindra Kumar Tyagi Established – 1989 Headquarters – Gurugram, Haryana PARLIAMENT NEWS Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla Constitutes ‘Parliamentary Friendship Groups’ with 64 Countries In February 2026, Om Birla, Speaker of Lok Sabha (the Lower House of Parliament) constituted ‘Parliamentary Friendship Groups (PFGs)’ with 64 countries to bolster inter-parliamentary cooperation and legislative dialogue. # Page 14^page=14
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 14 Current Affairs Study PDF About Parliamentary Friendship Groups: Significance: This new initiative will enable the Indian lawmakers to interact directly with their counterparts abroad, share legislative experience. • It will also facilitate regular dialogue, exchange of legislative practices, and will boost cooperation on trade, technology, culture, and shared global challenges. Structure: Each Parliamentary Friendship Group typically consisted of 11 members, with a designated Chairperson/Group Leader leading the group. Members: The groups comprise Members of Parliament (MPs) from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha across the political spectrum. • Senior leaders/ former Member of Parliaments (MPs): Ravi Shankar Prasad (Bharatiya Janata Party, BJP); M. People First: Humans must remain in control of AI systems. AI should strengthen human agency and protect societal values. Innovation over Restraint: Governance should encourage responsible innovation rather than restrict progress unnecessarily. Fairness & Equity: AI must avoid bias and discrimination, especially against vulnerable communities. Accountability: Developers and deployers must be responsible for AI outcomes. Understandable by Design: AI systems should provide clear explanations and disclosures. Safety, Resilience & Sustainability: AI must be secure, robust, environmentally responsible, and designed to minimise harm. Entitlement: Beneficiaries receive 5 kilogram (kg) free food grains per month in addition to entitlements under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, including wheat, rice, and millets for nutritional security, with portability via the ONORC system. About Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC): Definition: CBDCs are digital versions of a country’s fiat currency, issued and regulated by the central bank, providing a secure, state-backed alternative to cash while enhancing financial inclusion and reducing transaction costs. Legal: In India, CBDCs are governed by the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (RBI Act, 1934), amended through the Finance Bill 2022. Categories: Two types exist : Wholesale CBDC (e₹-W) for financial institutions and Retail CBDC (e₹-R) for everyday transactions by consumers and businesses. Pilot: India’s e-Rupee (e₹) pilot was launched in 2022–23, following global adoption trends like Sand Dollar (Bahamas, 2020), eNaira (Nigeria, 2020), and Digital Yuan/e-CNY (China, 2020 pilot). PE Expanded: A new concept of Service Permanent Establishment (Service PE) has been introduced, enabling certain service activities to constitute a taxable presence in a country. Stronger Information Sharing: The provisions on Exchange of Information have been updated and a new article on Assistance in Collection of Taxes has been introduced, strengthening cooperation between India and France in tackling tax evasion. Incorporation of BEPS Measures: The treaty now incorporates the relevant provisions of the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) – Multilateral Instrument (MLI), thereby aligning it with global anti-tax avoidance standards. About DTAC: Overview: A DTAC ensures that individuals and companies are not taxed twice on the same income in two countries. About Miniratna Status: Overview: The MoD grants Miniratna status to profit-making public sector companies to give them more autonomy and flexibility in decision making. It includes two categories, such as Category-I and Category-II. Miniratna Category-I: It is granted to well-performing public sector companies that have made profits consistently for the last 3 years and meet eligible financial criteria. • Approval: The Board of Directors (BoD) can spend up to Rs 500 crores on new projects, modernization, or equipment without government approval. • Eligibility: • The company must have made profits continuously for the last 3 years. • The company should have a net worth of at least Rs.500 crores or an average annual profit of Rs.30 crores or more over the past 3 years. • It must be a Schedule ‘A’ PSU, a well-established government company, and must demonstrate good operational performance and financial management. Miniratna Category-II: It is granted for public sector companies that are profitable but may not yet meet the higher financial criteria for Category-I. • Spending Capacity: The Board of Directors can spend up to Rs.100 crore on new projects, modernization, or equipment without government approval. • Autonomy: It provides more autonomy than regular PSUs but less than Category-I, helping the company grow while maintaining government oversight.
